facts.text: WSJ (via Odaily): the administration plans to announce, as early as this week, a multinational coalition to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz; whether escorts start before or after Iranian hostilities end is still undecided, and many countries remain noncommittal.

US tariffs: Trump said that, as the Supreme Court itself noted, he has 'absolute authority to impose tariffs in another form, and [has] already begun doing so', and called tariffs his most important decision.

Reuters (via Odaily): court papers unsealed Fri 13 Mar show Powell's lawyers told prosecutor Pirro on 29 Jan that Powell would not leave the Board after his chair term ends in May while he remains under investigation. A district judge (Boasberg) had blocked the DOJ subpoenas on Fri 13 Mar.

PAP week-ahead: the US-Israel war with Iran (from 28 Feb) and the Hormuz blockade keep oil around $100/bbl. On Sat 14 Mar Trump asked China, Japan, South Korea, France and the UK to send warships to Hormuz; US UN envoy Waltz said the US 'encourages, even demands' participation. The IEA said emergency stocks will start flowing soon (Asia/Oceania immediately, Europe/Americas end-March), part of the previously announced 400m-barrel release, the largest ever.

PAP week-ahead: all Reuters-polled economists expect the Fed to hold at 3.50-3.75% on 18 Mar; about two-thirds expect a cut to 3.25-3.50% next quarter, most likely June, right after Powell's term ends in May (Nomura: Warsh likely to deliver one or two cuts this year). FOMC decision and SEP 18 Mar 19:00 CET, presser 19:30.

PAP week-ahead: ECB decision Thu 19 Mar (14:15 CET). Last week Kocher (Austria) warned against acting hastily ('those who act hastily usually make mistakes'), Simkus (Lithuania) said the ECB should 'stick to our course' for now, and Muller (Estonia) urged a measured response while the ECB assesses whether the energy shock is temporary.

PAP week-ahead: BoE decides Thu 19 Mar. Reuters poll: most economists dropped calls for a March cut because of the energy shock; the market sees a cut to 3.50% in April or June; median year-end Bank Rate 3.25%. UBS (Turner) expects the next cut in April and two cuts this year. BoJ is expected to hold at 0.75% on 19 Mar, with a hike to 1.00% by end-June (Reuters poll; sources flag a possible April hike).

10Y closes 13 Mar (PAP/Bloomberg table): Bund 2.98%, OAT 3.67%, BTP 3.79%, Bonos 3.50%, gilt 4.82% -> OAT-Bund 69bp, BTP-Bund 81bp, Spain 52bp; Schatz 2.44%, gilt 2Y 4.13%; CZ10 4.96%, HU10 7.33%. One month earlier: Bund 2.76%, BTP 3.36%, gilt 4.42%. Live 06:36: UST10 4.26%, UST2 3.71%, JGB10 2.27%.

16 Mar morning: Brent May $104.89 (+$1.70) after a 3.3% gain on Friday; WTI Apr $99.34. Oil is up more than 40% in two weeks. CENTCOM struck more than 90 military targets on Kharg Island (oil infrastructure was not hit); Iran's FM Araghchi threatened US firms in the region if Iranian energy sites are attacked.

Treasury Sec. Bessent (via Jin10/Odaily): oil could be 'well below' $80 within months and inflation expectations are firmly anchored. Later (CNBC) he said the US is letting Iranian tankers pass through Hormuz, which helped oil fall.

16 Mar ~13:40: Reuters says oil loading at Fujairah (UAE) was halted again after a drone-strike fire; Israel launched wide strikes on Tehran and a limited ground operation in south Lebanon. DXY 99.94 (-0.4%), EUR/USD 1.1481, USD/JPY 159.08; UST10 4.24% (-4bp), 2s10s +56bp; Bund 10Y 2.95% (-4bp); Brent May $103.44; gold $5,011 (-1%), VIX 25.0.
US Feb industrial production +0.2% m/m vs +0.1% expected (Jan +0.7%); manufacturing +0.2% vs +0.1%; capacity utilisation 76.3% vs 76.2%. NAHB housing index Mar 38 vs 37 expected (Feb 37).

BofA (via Jin10): if the conflict runs into H2, Brent could average $130/bbl; after the war the market returns to oversupply, with Brent at $65 in 2027. Standard Chartered raised its 2026 Brent forecast to $85.5.
Trump said the Fed should 'immediately' convene a special meeting to cut rates.

16 Mar European close ~18:00: UST10 4.24% (-4bp), UST30 4.88%; Bund 10Y 2.95% (-3bp); DXY 100.0 (-0.36%), EUR/USD 1.1491, GBP/USD 1.3298; Brent May $102.69 (-0.5%), WTI Apr $96.10; TTF EUR50.17/MWh; gold $4,982 (-1.55%), silver $79.9. European stocks up ~0.4% (Commerzbank +9% on UniCredit's EUR35bn offer).

16 Mar: Trump said 'numerous countries' will help reopen Hormuz and that France (and possibly the UK) may help, but Germany, Greece and Norway ruled out military participation; Poland will not send troops. Trump said Iran is talking but 'not ready' for a deal and his China visit may be delayed. Araghchi: Iran did not propose a ceasefire and Hormuz is closed 'only to enemies'. Japan began releasing oil reserves. Kallas criticised US easing of Russian-oil sanctions as a 'dangerous precedent'. EU gas storage 29.0% vs 42.0% 5-yr avg. BofA: CEE central banks can wait and see; hikes only if oil goes above $150.

Wall Street closed higher 16 Mar (S&P 500 +1.0%) as oil fell after Bessent said Iranian tankers are allowed through Hormuz and the WSJ escort-coalition report; Brent May $100.24 (-2.8%), WTI Apr $93.52 (-5.2%) at 21:20.
The Trump administration asked Judge Boasberg to reconsider his ruling blocking the DOJ's criminal probe of Powell (Fed HQ renovation costs and his testimony), per court papers made public on 16 Mar.
RBA raised its cash rate 25bp to 4.10%, as expected (PAP).

10Y closes 16 Mar: Bund 2.95%, OAT 3.62%, BTP 3.73%, Bonos 3.44%, gilt 4.77% -> OAT-Bund 67bp, BTP-Bund 78bp, Spain 49bp; Schatz 2.40%; CZ10 4.89%, HU10 7.24%. Live 06:33: UST10 4.23%, UST2 3.68%, JGB10 2.27%.

17 Mar morning: Brent May $103.74 (+$3.49) after Monday's 2.8% fall, as Iran stepped up attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure (Odaily 09:25: a fire at a large UAE gas field, the first damage to the UAE's upstream facilities).
German ZEW expectations Mar -0.5 vs +39.2 expected (Feb 58.3), a collapse after the outbreak of the Iran war.

NEC director Hassett: the Iran conflict will end in the short term and tankers are starting to pass through Hormuz; further release of oil reserves can be considered; fertiliser is being imported from Venezuela to fill shortages.

PAP (LSEG data): markets price at least one ECB hike by year-end; hike bets have risen by more than 40bp since the conflict began. Van Lanschot (van Leenders): at $110 oil the market could price two ECB hikes; if Hormuz reopens, none. A hold on Thursday is widely expected.

BofA March fund manager survey: rate-cut expectations have cooled sharply; investors are raising cash at the fastest pace since March 2020; geopolitics and an inflation rebound replaced the 'AI bubble' as the biggest tail risk.
PAP FX/FI (dealer comment): the market now prices one Fed cut by year-end instead of two, and prices an ECB hike.

17 Mar: Israel said it killed Ali Larijani, head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council (Iran confirmed that evening), and Basij chief Gholamreza Soleimani. Trump said NATO made a 'very foolish mistake' and he no longer needs allies' help (Japan, Australia, South Korea included); Macron said France will not join a Hormuz operation; EU ministers showed no appetite to extend the Aspides mission. CNN: Iran sought a direct channel but Trump does not want to negotiate now; Axios: a Witkoff-Araghchi channel was re-established. Trump said his Beijing visit (planned 31 Mar-2 Apr) may slip about a month. Ukraine: the EU informally opened all six accession clusters; Zelensky accepted EU help to repair Druzhba (Brody pumping station fixed in ~1.5 months). Some US airports may close if DHS funding problems drag on.
Wall Street rose for a second day 17 Mar ahead of the Fed; Brent May $103.70 (+3.5%), WTI $96.13 at 21:09.

10Y closes 17 Mar: Bund 2.91%, OAT 3.56%, BTP 3.66%, Bonos 3.38%, gilt 4.69% -> OAT-Bund 65bp, BTP-Bund 75bp, Spain 47bp; Schatz 2.38%, gilt 2Y 4.04%; CZ10 4.76%, HU10 7.14%. Live 06:29: UST10 4.18%, UST2 3.66%, JGB10 2.22%.

18 Mar morning: Brent May $100.47 (-$2.76) after Iraq agreed to resume oil exports via Turkey, bypassing Hormuz. IMO: ~3,200 merchant ships with ~20,000 seafarers are trapped in the Gulf. Brent is up almost 70% year-to-date.
Kpler/JPMorgan (via Odaily): only about 2 tankers a day now transit Hormuz (vs ~100 before the war), with ~400 stranded; passage is selective and depends on political understandings with Tehran.
Euro-area Feb HICP (final) 1.9% y/y, unrevised from the flash (Jan 1.7%).
Trump asked 'when will Powell cut interest rates?' (Odaily headline only).
US Feb PPI +0.7% m/m vs +0.3% expected, 3.4% y/y vs 3.0%; ex food and energy +0.5% m/m vs +0.3% and 3.9% y/y vs 3.7%. Traders further reduced 2026 Fed cut bets (Odaily 13:41).

Trump waived Jones Act enforcement to curb high oil prices; Treasury eased sanctions on Venezuela's state oil company (PAP 21:15); Iran's IRGC issued evacuation warnings to energy facilities in several Gulf states after strikes on Iran's South Pars/Asaluyeh gas facilities.
US Jan durable goods 0.0% m/m (prelim 0.0%; Dec revised -0.9%); Jan factory orders +0.1% (in line). EIA crude stocks +6.16m bbl (exp +0.38m). Bank of Canada held at 2.25%, as expected.
PAP FX/FI: at end-February the market priced two and a half 25bp Fed cuts for 2026; it now prices only one. US inflation expectations rose by almost 0.8pp in March.

18 Mar European close ~18:00: UST10 4.22% (+3bp); Bund 10Y 2.94% (+4bp); DXY 99.83, EUR/USD 1.1507, USD/JPY 159.48; Brent May $108.44 (+5%), WTI $98.13; TTF EUR54.90 (+6.5%); gold $4,883 (-2.5%), silver $77.2. Iran published a list of Gulf energy sites it plans to hit after US/Israeli strikes on its gas industry.

FOMC (17-18 Mar) held the funds rate at 3.50-3.75%, 11-1, Miran dissenting for a 25bp cut (Waller voted with the majority). New statement line: 'The implications of developments in the Middle East for the U.S. economy are uncertain'; activity 'expanding at a solid pace', job gains low, unemployment little changed, inflation 'somewhat elevated'; easing-bias language kept ('extent and timing of additional adjustments').

SEP medians (vs Dec): funds rate 3.4% end-2026 (one cut, unchanged), 3.1% 2027, 3.1% 2028, longer run 3.1% (3.0%); GDP 2.4/2.3/2.1 (2.3/2.0/1.9); unemployment 4.4/4.3/4.2; PCE inflation 2.7/2.2/2.0 (2.4/2.1/2.0); core PCE 2.7/2.2/2.0 (2.5/2.1/2.0). 2026 dots: 7 at 3.625 (no cut), 7 at 3.375, 2 at 3.125, 2 at 2.875, 1 at 2.625; nobody above the current range for 2026; one 2027 dot implies a hike (3.875).

Powell press conference: the current stance is 'appropriate'; Middle East effects 'uncertain'; higher energy prices will lift headline inflation near term and some of the oil shock will show up in core; short-term inflation expectations rose while long-term ones stay anchored; policy is 'at the upper end' of the range between restrictive and not, which is the right starting point. A hike as the next move was discussed, but 'the vast majority' do not see it as their base case; he rejected the 'stagflation' label. He expects Feb PCE at 2.8% and core at 3.0%; no cuts without progress on inflation; the SEP looks like 'wild guesses'. He will stay as chair pro tempore if no successor is confirmed and will not leave the Board until the investigation is fully closed. After the presser DXY rose 0.54% to 100.12 and UST10 6bp to 4.26%.
Wall Street fell sharply 18 Mar to its lowest levels of 2026 as inflation fears returned; Brent May $109.79 (+6.2%), WTI $98.56 at 21:13. Israel said it killed Iran's intelligence minister Khatib.

18 Mar: Iran struck Qatar's main gas installation (fire contained); Iran's main gas plant at Bandar Kangan burned after US/Israeli strikes; CENTCOM used 2-ton penetrators on underground anti-ship missile stores near Hormuz. Merz: Germany will not join a military Hormuz mission while the war lasts. DNI Gabbard said Iran's enrichment programme had been fully neutralised in 2025 and not resumed. Orban will block the EUR90bn EU loan to Ukraine until Druzhba flows resume; Slovakia imposed diesel rationing and higher prices for foreigners; Vance to visit Hungary before the April election.
WSJ's Timiraos (via Odaily, 'Fed mouthpiece'): Powell's comments restrict Trump's 'room to manoeuvre' at the Fed (headline only).

Trump said he did not know about Israel's strike on Iran's South Pars field and warned that if Iran hits Qatar's LNG facilities again the US will 'blow up' the whole of South Pars. Israeli officials told Reuters the strike was coordinated with the US but probably will not be repeated.

10Y closes 18 Mar (FOMC day): Bund 2.94%, OAT 3.60%, BTP 3.73%, Bonos 3.44%, gilt 4.74% -> OAT-Bund 66bp, BTP-Bund 79bp, Spain 50bp; Schatz 2.44%, gilt 2Y 4.10%; CZ10 4.80%, HU10 7.14%. Live 06:36 (post-FOMC): UST10 4.27%, UST2 3.80% (3.77 prior), JGB10 2.26%.
19 Mar morning: Brent May $113.10 (+$5.33) after attacks on key Gulf energy sites; Karobaar Capital: $140-160 Brent 'would not be madness'.
UK ILO unemployment 5.2% (3m to Jan) vs 5.3% expected (prior 5.2%).
SNB held at 0.00% and the Riksbank at 1.75% (as expected); BoJ held at 0.75% (PAP).
19 Mar ~09:45: European stocks sharply lower; gold $4,734 (-1.7%); Brent $114.47 (+$6.60); UST10 4.27%; EUR/USD 1.1459.

Bloomberg (via PAP): Brent May +6.5% to $114.38 and TTF +16.5% to EUR63.47/MWh as Gulf attacks threaten long-lasting damage to major energy facilities. QatarEnergy (al-Kaabi): Iranian strikes knocked out 17% of Qatar's LNG export capacity (~$20bn a year in losses).

BoE MPC (meeting ended 18 Mar) voted 9-0 to hold Bank Rate at 3.75% (Feb was 5-4). Summary: Middle East conflict has sharply raised energy prices; CPI will be higher near term; the MPC is 'alert to the increased risk' of second-round effects, which rise the longer energy prices stay high, and 'stands ready to act as necessary'. Minutes: CPI seen close to 3.5% in March and 3-3.5% over the next couple of quarters (Q3 up to ~3.5%, vs ~2% expected in Feb); the market-implied Bank Rate path 'increased significantly'. Jin10 called it a 'hawkish pause' (a 7-2 hold had been seen as more likely).

Bessent: the US will not attack Iran's energy infrastructure and will use Iranian oil to lower prices; later (Fox Business) he said the administration is weighing lifting sanctions on ~140m bbl of Iranian oil already on tankers and accused China of supporting Iran.

PAP (LSEG): investors no longer price a Fed cut this year; LSEG data point to a cut in mid-2027. Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and Barclays moved their first-cut call to September from June. UST10 4.30% (+4bp), Bund 10Y 3.00% (+6bp) at 13:29; Brent $114.

US initial claims 205k vs 215k expected (prior 213k), lowest since the week to 10 Jan; continuing 1.857m vs 1.852m. Philly Fed Mar +18.1 (Feb +12.6). Jan new home sales 587k saar vs 722k expected (Dec revised 712k); Feb Conference Board LEI -0.1% (in line); Jan wholesale inventories -0.5% (prelim +0.2%).
Spot gold fell below $4,600/oz (intraday loss ~4%; silver -8%), new lows since 6 Feb.

ECB held again: DFR 2.00%, MRO 2.15%, MLF 2.40%; unanimous (Lagarde: 'no divergence of views'). The war 'has made the outlook significantly more uncertain, creating upside risks for inflation and downside risks for economic growth' and will have 'a material impact on near-term inflation' via energy; medium-term effects depend on the intensity and duration of the conflict; meeting-by-meeting, no pre-commitment. Staff also published adverse and severe war scenarios. After the decision EUR/USD rose to 1.1485 and Bund 10Y 5bp to 2.99%.

ECB staff projections (cut-off unusually late, 11 Mar): HICP 2.6% 2026, 2.0% 2027, 2.1% 2028 (Dec 1.9/1.8/2.0); core 2.3/2.2/2.1; GDP 0.9/1.3/1.4 (Dec 1.2/1.4/1.4). Adverse scenario HICP 3.5/2.1/1.6, GDP 0.6/1.2/1.6; severe scenario HICP 4.4/4.8/2.8, GDP 0.4/0.9/1.9. Assumptions: oil $81.3/72.1/70.2, gas EUR46.4/36.6/26.1/MWh, USD/EUR 1.16. PAP also gives Feb final core HICP at 2.4% y/y (Jan 2.2%).

CNB held the 2W repo at 3.50% (discount 2.50%, Lombard 4.50%), 7-0. CZ Feb CPI 1.4% y/y was the lowest in ten years; the updated forecast (partly reflecting higher oil) has headline below 2% this year and close to target next year, with core elevated. 'Relatively tight' policy is still needed (credit and money growth, tight labour market, wages 7.4% y/y in Q4). Middle East effects do not jeopardise the low-inflation environment and 'do not generate pressure for an immediate reaction'; risks balanced overall.

Lagarde press conference: the energy price rise will push inflation above 2% in the short term and, if it persists, could broaden via indirect and second-round effects, which need close monitoring; market-based short-term inflation expectations rose markedly, while most long-term measures stay around 2%; she would not say the ECB is 'in a good place', but its position is 'appropriate'; growth risks tilted down, inflation risks up; government energy support must be 'temporary, targeted and tailored'. After the presser EUR/USD rose 0.69% to 1.1529 and Bund 10Y +1bp to 2.95%.

19 Mar: France, the UK, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands and Japan said they are 'ready to contribute' to Hormuz security; Trump, meeting PM Takaichi, said Japan is stepping up unlike NATO and ruled out ground troops; Merz welcomed signals that Washington is ready to end hostilities. Iran's parliament is weighing transit fees for Hormuz; NATO is suspending its Iraq training mission. EU summit: 25 states backed Ukraine conclusions, but Orban still blocks the EUR90bn loan. EU gas storage 28.9% vs 41.5% 5-yr avg.

Wall Street fell for a second day 19 Mar; oil's gains slowed late: Brent May $107.36 (-0.05%), WTI $94.96 at 21:27. Late in New York the DXY fell more than 1% as global central banks signalled vigilance (Odaily 22:56); Brazil cut only 25bp to 14.75%.
Netanyahu said Israel will 'suspend' strikes on Iranian energy facilities (Odaily headline).

10Y closes 19 Mar (ECB/BoE day; PAP table without date stamps): Bund 2.96%, OAT 3.64%, BTP 3.78%, Bonos 3.47%, gilt 4.84% -> OAT-Bund 68bp, BTP-Bund 82bp, Spain 51bp; Schatz 2.59% (+15bp), gilt 2Y 4.40% (+30bp); CZ2 4.14%, CZ10 4.85%, HU10 7.32%. UST10 4.25%, UST2 3.79%, JGB10 2.28%.

Nagel (Bloomberg): the ECB will have to consider a hike as soon as next month if war-driven price pressure grows; a worse medium-term outlook and durably higher expectations 'probably mean the need for a more restrictive policy'. Makhlouf did not rule out an April hike but said it cannot be predicted (PAP 11:43). Bloomberg: the ECB sent European banks queries on risks, liquidity and client behaviour linked to the Middle East.

PAP: investors fully price three euro-area hikes this year. JPMorgan now expects ECB hikes in April and July; Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank expect June and September (DB: DFR to 2.5%, the top of the neutral range; MS then sees cuts back to 2% in June and September 2027).

Governor Bowman still expects three cuts in 2026 and will monitor leverage in the AI sector. Governor Waller: he had planned to dissent for a cut after the -92k Feb payrolls, but the Hormuz blockade means oil stays high for longer and would eventually pass into core, so he wants to wait before deciding on cuts later this year; he would support cuts if conditions improve.

IEA (Birol): the conflict could cause the largest supply disruption in oil-market history, and normal Gulf oil and gas flows may take up to six months to restore; it urged immediate demand-side measures. Iran said no crude-laden tanker transited Hormuz in the past 24 hours (Odaily 14:50); US media say three more warships and thousands of troops are heading to the region.
Jin10: traders see a 50% probability of a Fed hike by October; STIR futures imply a likely hike in December (Odaily 15:16). DXY 99.69 (+0.5%) at 15:17; spot gold below $4,580, silver below $69.

20 Mar ~18:00: Bund and gilt 10Y at their highest since 2011 and 2008 (above 3% and 5%), up 7bp and 16bp intraday; Brent briefly above $120 this week, the highest since mid-2022, about +5% w/w; gold heading for its worst week since 1983 (-9% at ~18:00). After the ECB/BoE/SNB meetings markets fully price 3 ECB hikes by end-2026, about 75% odds of an April hike, a 25bp BoE hike by June, and a 50% chance of a Fed hike by October. UST10 4.38% (+13bp), Bund 10Y 3.05% (+9bp); DXY 99.6, EUR/USD ~1.155, USD/JPY 159.3; Brent May $109.8.

Wall Street fell sharply 20 Mar (fourth straight weekly loss) as Reuters reported Iraq declared force majeure on all foreign-operated oilfields; LSEG: Fed cut bets pushed from Dec 2026 into 2027; Brent May $111.70 (+2.8%), WTI $98.81 at 21:20. PAP also says Brent topped $122 intraday, which conflicts with its own quotes; treat that figure with caution.

S&P upgraded Ireland to AA+ from AA (outlook Stable; previously AA/Positive), the first upgrade since May 2023 and Ireland's highest rating with any major agency (Irish Times, 20 Mar; agency release Fri evening, 23:00 is a placeholder).

Trump (Truth Social, 20 Mar US time) said the US is 'considering gradually winding down' its major military operations as it nears its goals (degrade missiles and launchers, the defence industrial base, navy and air force; no nuclear capability; protect Gulf allies), and that other countries using Hormuz should guard it.
US Treasury issued a 30-day, narrowly scoped licence allowing the sale of Iranian crude and products loaded by 20 Mar (~140m bbl at sea).
Gold's largest weekly drop since March 1983: spot $4,491.67 at the 20 Mar NY close (-3.4% d/d, over -10% w/w); silver $67.90 (-15% w/w).
BofA: a Fed hike this year cannot be ruled out but needs a stable labour market, further inflation intensification and Powell remaining chair. HSBC (21 Mar) expects the Fed on hold in 2026 and 2027.

Trump ultimatum (Sat 21 Mar evening US time): unless Iran fully opens Hormuz within 48 hours (to ~01:00 CET Tue 24 Mar), the US will destroy its power plants. Iran (Ghalibaf, IRGC) replied it would close Hormuz completely and treat regional energy infrastructure, and US-linked firms, as legitimate targets.
Bessent: '50 days of price increases' (an offhand figure; it could be 30 or 100) can be traded for '50 years' of a nuclear-free Iran.

Weekend 21-22 Mar: G7 FMs said they are ready to act to protect energy supplies; the EC urged lower gas-storage targets for next winter; Iran fired two IRBMs at Diego Garcia (missed, per WSJ) and hit Dimona and Arad; US/Israel struck Natanz; Axios: the US expects 2-3 more weeks of fighting while advisers prepare diplomacy; Japan's tankers may get passage. Ukraine-US talks in Florida (Zelensky: the key is whether Russia wants peace). Elections: CDU won Rhineland-Palatinate (ARD exit poll 30.5%); Slovenia exit polls put PM Golob's Freedom Movement first. Moody's completed a periodic review of Poland with no rating action (A2/negative).
CME FedWatch (Sunday night): April +25bp hike 12.4%, hold 87.6%; by June cumulative +25bp 21.9%, +50bp 1.6%, hold 76.5%.

10Y closes 20 Mar: Bund 3.04%, OAT 3.76%, BTP 3.96%, Bonos 3.58%, gilt 4.99% -> OAT-Bund 72bp, BTP-Bund 92bp, Spain 54bp; Schatz 2.67%, gilt 2Y 4.57%; CZ10 4.85%, HU10 7.29%. Live 06:31: UST10 4.41%, UST2 3.94%, JGB10 2.31%.

PAP week-ahead: about 30 Fed/ECB/BoE/SNB speeches; after last week's meetings, euro-area hike expectations jumped and expected US cuts were priced out. ING (Knightley): central banks will talk up hikes hoping words do some work; actually hiking would be risky. Flash PMIs Tue; MNB Tue (hold at 6.25% expected); rating reviews after Fri close: Italy (Moody's), Spain (Moody's), Czechia (S&P), Denmark, Bulgaria, Switzerland (Fitch).

Asia sold off 23 Mar after the ultimatum and 'unprecedented' explosions in Tehran; spot gold fell below $4,150 (-7.8% on the day; below $4,100 at 08:25), wiping out its year-to-date gain; Brent May $113.46 at 07:55, up more than 50% since the war began.
Gilt 10Y opened +6bp at 5.065%, the highest since 2008; 30Y 5.632%. UST2 touched 4.00% (+10bp intraday), the highest since June 2025 (Odaily 11:08).

Trump (Truth Social, ~12:10 CET): after 'very good and productive' talks with Iran over two days, he told the Pentagon to postpone strikes on Iran's power plants and energy infrastructure for five days. Brent May fell as much as ~13.6% to $96.69 and WTI briefly below $83; UST10 fell 8.4bp to 4.307%; gold rebounded more than $100.
Chicago Fed's Goolsbee: there may be situations in which rate hikes are needed (Jin10 headline).

Trump: the sides agreed 'main points of an agreement' and the war could end soon; Hormuz could be jointly controlled; he is not talking to the Supreme Leader. Iran's MFA confirmed a US offer to negotiate via 'friendly states' but denied any talks; Ghalibaf called the reports false news used to manipulate oil and financial markets. Turkey, Egypt and Pakistan relay messages; a meeting in Islamabad is being pushed.

Goldman Sachs raised its 12-month US recession probability to 30% (+5pp) and its end-2026 unemployment forecast to 4.6%; it still sees Fed cuts in September and December; it raised its oil forecasts, calling the Hormuz disruption the largest supply shock in oil-market history.

23 Mar European close: UST10 4.36% (-2bp); Bund 10Y 3.00% (-4bp); DXY 99.32 (-0.33%), EUR/USD 1.1599, USD/JPY 158.60; Brent May $102.0 (-9%), WTI $90.38; TTF EUR54.90 (as quoted; the same figure as 18 Mar, possibly stale).

Italy: Meloni's government narrowly lost the two-day referendum on its judicial reform (RAI exit poll: 49-53% against vs 47-51% for). Slovenia election: Golob's Freedom Movement 28.54% vs Jansa's SDS 28.17% (99.45% counted). CDU won Rhineland-Palatinate (31%, SPD 25.9%, AfD 19.5%). The FT reported the US warned the EU it could lose 'favourable' LNG access if it does not adopt the trade deal; EU-Mercosur provisional application from 1 May.
Wall Street rallied 23 Mar (Dow +600pts) on Trump's talk of negotiations; Brent May $99.80 (-11%), WTI $88.77 at 21:27.

10Y closes 23 Mar: Bund 3.01%, OAT 3.71%, BTP 3.88%, Bonos 3.52%, gilt 4.92% -> OAT-Bund 70bp, BTP-Bund 87bp, Spain 51bp; Schatz 2.58%, gilt 2Y 4.42%; CZ10 4.79%, HU10 7.46%. Live 06:30: UST10 4.38%, UST2 3.90%, JGB10 2.28%.

24 Mar morning: Brent May $102.71 (+$2.77) after Monday's 11% drop, on fears other countries could join the war; gold rebounded above $4,400 (Odaily 08:07). Kpler (AFP): Hormuz transits fell 95% in March (144 crossings 1-23 Mar vs ~138 a day before the war).

EZ flash PMIs Mar: composite 50.5 vs 51.0 expected (Feb 51.9), a 10-month low; services 50.1 vs 51.1 (51.9); manufacturing 51.4 vs 49.6 (50.8). New orders contracted for the first time in eight months; input-cost inflation fastest since Feb 2023, output prices fastest since Feb 2024; confidence had its steepest drop since Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Germany: manufacturing 51.7 vs 49.5, services 51.2 (53.5). France: manufacturing 50.2 vs 49.5, services 48.3 (49.6).
UK flash PMIs Mar: manufacturing 51.4 vs 50.0 expected (Feb 51.7); services 51.2 vs 52.9 (53.9).

Iran presented five ceasefire demands to the US and is levying 'security transit fees' on some ships (Odaily 13:55); the IRGC says all vessels must coordinate with it, and Iran says non-hostile ships may pass after coordination (FT, 22:30). Saudi Arabia and the UAE are reportedly considering joining action against Iran.

MNB held the base rate at 6.25% (corridor 5.25-7.25%), as expected. Brent briefly neared $120 and European gas is up 70%+ since the war began. Feb CPI 1.4% (core 2.1%); the new forecast sees inflation above the tolerance band from Q3 and back at target sustainably only in H2 2027 (3.8% avg 2026, 3.7% 2027); GDP 1.7% 2026. FX stability is key; on 10 Mar the MNB began meeting FX needs for energy imports; 'careful and patient' policy, tight conditions warranted. Goldman (PAP 23 Mar): without the war the MNB would probably have cut again in March.
24 Mar ~14:30: futures reversed lower after Iran denied any talks with Trump; UST10 4.39% (+5bp), Bund 10Y 3.03% (+1bp); DXY 99.43, EUR/USD 1.1576; Brent May $102.95 (+3%).
US flash S&P Global PMIs Mar: manufacturing 52.4 vs 51.5 expected (Feb 51.6); services 51.1 vs 52.0 (51.7); composite 51.4 vs 51.9 (51.9).

24 Mar: Trump said Iran agreed it will never obtain a nuclear weapon and that Tehran sent a 'very significant present' related to Hormuz. Denmark election (exit poll): Social Democrats first with 19.2%, neither bloc has a majority. Russia used a record 948 drones on Ukraine in a day; the EC said Slovakia's diesel curbs for foreigners breach EU law.

Wall Street fell 24 Mar as oil and Treasury yields rose after a 2-year auction BMO called weak; Brent May $99.98, WTI $88.40 at 22:13 (earlier ~$104 at 18:00). EUR/USD 1.1583, USD/JPY 158.9 before 18:00.
Washington Post (via Odaily): court records show a senior aide to DOJ's Pirro admitted in a closed hearing this month that there is no evidence of wrongdoing by Powell in the Fed HQ renovation probe.
Odaily: spot gold $4,550 (+1.7%) at 01:12 and above $4,600 (+2.8%) at 04:53 on 25 Mar; WTI below $88.

Trump (24 Mar, DHS swearing-in; PAP 25 Mar): he held off striking 'one of the largest power plants in the world' because 'we are negotiating'; Witkoff, Kushner, Rubio and Vance are in the talks; he thinks he will end the war soon and that 'regime change' has effectively happened.

10Y closes 24 Mar (~18:00 stamps): Bund 3.03%, OAT 3.76%, BTP 3.95%, Bonos 3.56%, gilt 4.96% -> OAT-Bund 73bp, BTP-Bund 92bp, Spain 53bp; Schatz 2.67%, gilt 2Y 4.47%; CZ10 4.88%, HU10 7.47%. UST10 4.38%, UST2 3.91% (18:00 24 Mar); JGB10 2.27%.

NYT: the US sent Iran a 15-point plan to end the war via Pakistan. Brent May fell to $100.22 (-$4.09) at 07:44 and below $100 by ~09:00. Iran's initial reaction was 'not positive' (Reuters); WSJ: Iran demands the closure of US Gulf bases, an end to Israeli strikes on Hezbollah, reparations and the lifting of all sanctions; Leavitt: Trump is ready to 'unleash hell' if Iran does not accept defeat.

UK Feb CPI 3.0% y/y (unchanged; in line with expectations per Trading Economics), +0.4% m/m; core 3.2% (Jan 3.1%, an unexpected rise); services 4.3% (4.4%); goods 1.6%; CPIH 3.2%. Clothing pushed up, motor fuels pulled down; the data pre-date the war's energy shock.
German Ifo Mar 86.4 vs 86.3 expected (Feb revised 88.4 from 88.6).

Lagarde: the ECB will act 'decisively and quickly' if the energy-cost rise threatens a broader inflation wave, but it is still assessing the shock (PAP). Per the PAP 30 Mar week-ahead she also said the ECB is ready to change policy at any meeting if needed and must identify early when the shock risks broadening, but will not act before it has enough data. The 12:00 clock is a placeholder.
PAP (CME FedWatch): markets price no Fed easing this year, vs two cuts priced before the war. Bund 10Y 2.96% (-6bp), UST10 4.34% at 14:02.

Iran publicly set five ceasefire conditions ('accept the conditions first, then negotiate') and called the 15-point plan 'another lie'; Pakistan has passed the US proposals to Iran; Vance may travel to Pakistan; House Speaker said the US will not conduct ground combat in Iran. The White House said Trump's China visit will be 14-15 May.

25 Mar European close: UST10 4.31% (-5bp), UST30 4.89%; Bund 10Y 2.95% (-7bp); DXY 99.51, EUR/USD 1.1569, USD/JPY 159.23; Brent May $101.14 (-3.2%), WTI $90.0; TTF EUR52.46 (-3%). Gold ~$4,550-4,600 (+1.7-2.8% intraday per PAP/Odaily).

25 Mar: Hungary halts gas deliveries to Ukraine until Druzhba oil flows resume (Orban); Fidesz's Lazar floated a post-election coalition with Mi Hazank; Guterres warned the war is spiralling out of control; CBS: US intelligence detected two types of IRGC mines in Hormuz. US EIA crude stocks +6.93m bbl; the IEA is ready to release more reserves.
Wall Street rose moderately 25 Mar on hopes for easing of the Iran war; Brent May $102.80 (-1.6%), WTI $91.09 at 21:13.

10Y closes 25 Mar: Bund 2.96%, OAT 3.65%, BTP 3.84%, Bonos 3.47%, gilt 4.84% -> OAT-Bund 69bp, BTP-Bund 88bp, Spain 51bp; Schatz 2.60%, gilt 2Y 4.41%; CZ10 4.81%, HU10 7.36%. Live 06:30: UST10 4.36%, UST2 3.92%, JGB10 2.28%.
26 Mar morning: Brent May $104.29 (+$2.03) on conflicting US/Iran signals; it topped $114 earlier this week.
German GfK consumer climate (Apr) -28.0 vs -27.3 expected (prior -24.8); France consumer confidence Mar 89 (Feb 91); INSEE business climate 97 (unchanged).
Norges Bank held its policy rate at 4.00%.
EBRD: oil above $100 and supply-chain disruption could cut global GDP growth by at least 0.4pp and add more than 1.5pp to inflation.

The European Parliament approved the EU-US trade deal (zero tariffs on US industrial goods; 15% cap on most EU goods) with amendments: no implementation until the US meets its commitments, and expiry in March 2028 unless extended; trilogue with member states next. The US recently opened new investigations into major partners incl. the EU and China to replace the struck-down reciprocal tariffs; the EU wants clarity on cuts to the 50% steel/aluminium-content tariffs.
Reuters poll: 65 of 82 economists (79%) expect one or two Fed cuts this year; PCE inflation seen averaging 3.3% in Q2, 3.1% in Q3 and 2.9% in Q4.
US initial claims 210k vs 210k expected (prior 205k).
Nagel (Reuters): 'by April we will have enough data' to decide whether to act or wait. Bund 10Y 3.05% (+9bp), UST10 4.38% at 13:54; Brent May $107.
Bessent: the dollar has re-established its safe-haven status as capital flows in.

26 Mar European close: Bund 10Y 3.07% (+11bp), UST10 4.38% (+7bp), UST30 4.95%; DXY 99.58, EUR/USD 1.1532, USD/JPY 159.66; Brent May $108.85 (+6.4%), WTI $95.08; TTF EUR55.42 (+5%); spot gold below $4,400 (Odaily 17:31).

26 Mar: Witkoff confirmed the 15-point plan went via Pakistan and Iran delivered its formal reply through intermediaries; Trump said Iran is 'begging' for a deal but he is unsure one is possible; WSJ: he wants the war over within weeks; Trump floated taking control of Iranian oil 'as in Venezuela' and said Iran let 10 tankers through as a 'gift'. Kallas: reports of US pressure on Ukraine to cede territory are worrying. Reuters: Russian oil-export capacity is down at least 40% after Ukrainian strikes. The Bundestag passed a law limiting fuel-price changes to once a day.
Wall Street fell sharply 26 Mar as Treasury 2Y and 10Y yields jumped with oil; Brent May $105.65 (+3.3%), WTI $92.97 at 21:34.
Trump postponed strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure by a further 10 days, to 20:00 ET on Mon 6 Apr, saying talks are progressing well; 6 April becomes the binary catalyst for markets.

10Y closes 26 Mar (unstamped PAP table): Bund 3.07%, OAT 3.80%, BTP 4.02%, Bonos 3.61%, gilt 4.97% -> OAT-Bund 73bp, BTP-Bund 95bp, Spain 54bp; Schatz 2.72%, gilt 2Y 4.53%; CZ10 4.87%, HU10 7.31%. UST10 4.43%, UST2 3.99%; JGB10 2.38%.
UK Feb retail sales incl. fuel -0.4% m/m vs -0.7% expected (Jan revised +2.0%); GfK consumer confidence Mar -21 vs -24 expected (Feb -19).

Bund 10Y rose to 3.087%, the highest since 2011 (Jin10); OAT 10Y 3.876% (+8bp), the highest since June 2009 (10:11); JGB10 2.38%, the highest since 1999, and JGB30 3.71% (07:25-08:47); UST30 4.986%, the highest since September 2025 (14:07).
Spain flash Mar HICP 3.3% y/y (Feb 2.5%), the highest since June 2024 but 0.5pp below expectations; fuels drove the rise.

Fed Governor Cook (26 Mar evening speech, reported by PAP 27 Mar): the oil spike changed the balance of risks, making inflation a bigger concern than employment. Brent May $109.79 (+1.7%); Brent rose a record ~49% in March.

IRGC: Hormuz is closed and any passage faces 'severe measures'; ships to or from ports of US/Israeli allies are banned (Reuters). Israel upgraded and widened its strikes; Iran threatened steel plants in Israel and the Gulf; Iran's Arak heavy-water reactor and the Ardakan yellowcake plant were hit.
LSEG: probability of an ECB hike in April 71%. UST10 4.46% (+5bp), Bund 10Y 3.11% at 13:55; DXY 100.10; Brent May $111.21.
UMich sentiment Mar final 55.3 (prelim 55.5; Feb 56.6); 1-year inflation expectations 3.8% vs 3.4% expected and prior; 5-10-year 3.2% (prior 3.3%).

Rubio: the Iran war should end within weeks (insider report); Iran may set up a Hormuz toll system; the US can achieve its goals without ground forces. Wadephul: the US and Iran held indirect talks and plan to meet in Pakistan. WSJ: Trump is considering sending 10,000 more troops. The UN set up a Hormuz task force; the UAE wants to join a Hormuz task force (FT).
Wunsch: the ECB will have to hike if the war does not end by June, though patience is needed now; he is comfortable with markets pricing at least two hikes this year.

27 Mar ~18:00: European stocks down more than 9% month-to-date; Nasdaq in correction; Bund 10Y 3.10% (+2bp), UST10 ~4.42%; USD/JPY above 160 for the first time since 2024 (JPY -2.7% in March; 161.95 would be the weakest since 1986, raising intervention talk); DXY 100.10; gold $4,550 (+3%); Brent May $111.5 (+3.2%), WTI $98.5. Brent is up ~48% in March, a record monthly gain (Bloomberg via PAP 08:32).
Wall Street fell hard again 27 Mar (Dow -~800pts, into correction) as hopes for a quick end to the war faded; Brent May $113.38 (+5%), WTI $99.94 at 21:20.

Scheduled Friday-evening sovereign reviews (PAP calendar): Italy and Spain (Moody's), Czechia (S&P), Denmark, Bulgaria, Switzerland (Fitch). The countryeconomy histories show no rating or outlook change for any of them in March. Moody's stays at Italy Baa2/Stable and Spain A3/Stable. LaPresse (28 Mar) says Moody's cut its Italy 2026 GDP forecast to 0.7% (from 0.8%) and raised 2026 inflation to 2.1% (from 1.8%). No press releases were retrieved, so the outcomes (affirmation or no action) are unconfirmed; the clock is a placeholder.
Thailand and Iran agreed to let ships pass through Hormuz; two more India-bound LPG tankers left the Gulf (28 Mar).

US officials (via Jin10): the Pentagon is preparing for weeks of ground operations in Iran (Washington Post: special forces and infantry; options include seizing Kharg Island or coastal areas near Hormuz; no White House decision yet).

Weekend 28-29 Mar: Houthis confirmed missile attacks on Israel, formally joining the war; Iran struck the UAE and Bahrain overnight after US/Israeli strikes on civilian infrastructure; Ghalibaf threatened to 'set fire' to US troops if they land; an Iranian MP said Iran is considering leaving the NPT; Ukrainian drones hit Russia's Ust-Luga port again; 'No Kings' protests drew a record turnout in the US.

FT interview (Sun 29 Mar): Trump said what he most wants is to 'take the oil in Iran' and he may seize Kharg Island (90% of Iran's exports); indirect talks via a Pakistani envoy are going well and a deal is expected soon; '3,000 targets left' after 13,000 hit; Iran's tanker 'gift' rose to 20 ships; Ghalibaf is the chief Iranian interlocutor. Trump also said Iran has met 'most' of the 15 points (Air Force One, 03:02); Iran publicly rejects them. Clock is Warsaw time (CEST from 29 Mar).
Punchbowl (via Odaily): the Senate Banking Committee plans Warsh's Fed-chair confirmation hearing as early as the week of 13 April, provided his paperwork is complete.

10Y closes 27 Mar: Bund 3.09%, OAT 3.83%, BTP 4.05%, Bonos 3.63%, gilt 4.97% -> OAT-Bund 74bp, BTP-Bund 96bp, Spain 54bp; Schatz 2.67%, gilt 2Y 4.48%; CZ10 4.96%, HU10 7.33%. Live 06:32: UST10 4.39%, UST2 3.88%, JGB10 2.37%. On Friday UST10 broke above ~4.40% and Bund above ~3.05% (PKO BP).

PAP week-ahead: on Fri 27 Mar afternoon markets cut ECB hike bets: April +25bp odds fell to 50% (a week earlier a full April hike plus one more by year-end was priced) after Schnabel said there is no need to rush or overreact. De Guindos: de-anchoring of inflation expectations would trigger action (Feb data showed expectations easing towards 2%). Commerzbank expects an April hike, but probably only one; BofA sees a 'sizeable' chance of an April hike. The Bloomberg consensus for EZ Mar flash HICP (31 Mar) is 2.6% (core 2.4%), which would be the highest since March 2022. US Mar payrolls Fri 3 Apr (consensus +51k after -92k; unemployment 4.4%); US retail sales and ISM on 1 Apr. Filed by the article's date (conservative; Schnabel spoke Fri 27 Mar).
Nomura moved its Fed cut calls to September and December (from June and September), citing war-driven inflation risks and the delayed Warsh confirmation; it still sees a dovish bias.
EZ economic sentiment Mar 96.6 vs 96.5 expected (Feb revised 98.2).

Trump: talks have made 'significant progress', but if no deal is reached and Hormuz is not opened, the US will hit all power plants, oil wells, Kharg Island and possibly desalination plants. Iran's first VP: Hormuz talks need a US commitment not to invade; Rubio: Iran will never be allowed to control Hormuz permanently. Iran struck a Kuwaiti power plant; Saudi Arabia intercepted five ballistic missiles.
German flash Mar HICP 2.8% y/y vs 2.8% expected (Feb 2.0%).
Governor Miran: inflation expectations are not yet affected by higher oil; the Fed's balance sheet is too large and he wants to shrink it (Jin10).
DXY touched 100.56, the highest since May 2025 (Odaily); ING: the dollar firms again on war-escalation fears.

Powell (Harvard lecture): the Fed is 'in a good position to wait and see' how the war affects the economy and inflation; policymakers usually look through supply shocks but must watch expectations, which look 'well anchored beyond the short term'; it is too early to judge the size of the energy shock, so the Fed is not yet facing the question of how to respond. DXY 100.54 (+0.34%), UST10 4.33% (-11bp) after his remarks. Jin10: hike bets have been withdrawn and markets are again pricing the possibility of cuts this year.

30 Mar European close: UST10 4.33% (-11bp), UST30 4.90%; Bund 10Y 3.03% (-6bp); DXY 100.51 (+0.31%), EUR/USD 1.1455 (-0.46%), USD/JPY 159.42; Brent May $112.44, WTI $100.86; TTF EUR54.84; gold ~$4,540-4,569 (Odaily). Morgan Stanley cut global equities to equal-weight, citing flows into US stocks and bonds as a safe haven.

30 Mar: G7 finance and energy ministers and central-bank governors said they are ready to take all necessary steps to keep energy markets stable; EU energy ministers meet Tue 31 Mar on a joint response to fuel prices (EC 'toolbox'); a Woodside LNG plant in Australia is still down after a cyclone; Zelensky is ready for an Easter truce.
Wall Street fell 30 Mar on higher oil and a sharp tech drop and took Powell calmly; Brent May $114.17 (+1.4%), WTI Apr $104.22 at 22:13.

fed_pricing.text: Economists (Reuters poll): all expect a hold on 18 Mar; ~2/3 expect the first cut to 3.25-3.50% in Q2, most likely June (forecasts, not market pricing).
BoE (Reuters poll): market expects a cut to 3.50% in April or June; median year-end Bank Rate 3.25%.
ECB (LSEG): at least one ECB hike priced by year-end; hike bets up >40bp since the war began.
Market prices one Fed cut by end-2026 instead of two, and an ECB hike (PAP dealer comment).
After the hot Feb PPI, traders further reduced 2026 Fed cut bets (Odaily).
End-Feb: ~2.5 Fed cuts priced for 2026; 18 Mar (pre-FOMC): only one (PAP).
CME FedWatch pre-decision: March hold 98.9%, +25bp 1.1%, cut 0%; by April cut 2.0% / hold 96.9% / hike 1.0%; by June cut 16.3% / hold 82.5% / hike 0.9%.
CME FedWatch post-FOMC: April hold 100%; by June cumulative -25bp 11.2%, hold 88.8%; by July hold 77.4%.
LSEG: no Fed cut priced for 2026; first cut priced around mid-2027. MS, GS and Barclays moved their first-cut forecast to September (PAP); Odaily 13:35: traders no longer expect a 2026 cut.
ECB: three euro-area hikes in 2026 fully priced (PAP).
Fed: ~50% probability of a hike by October; STIR futures imply a likely hike by December (Jin10 via Odaily, 15:04/15:16).
Close 20 Mar: ECB 3 hikes by end-2026 fully priced, April hike ~75%; BoE 25bp hike priced for June; Fed 50% chance of a hike by October (PAP).
CME FedWatch: April +25bp 12.4% / hold 87.6%; by June +25bp 21.9%, +50bp 1.6%, hold 76.5%.
CME FedWatch (via PAP): no Fed easing priced this year, vs two cuts before the war.
Reuters poll: 65 of 82 economists expect 1-2 Fed cuts in 2026 (forecasts).
CME FedWatch: April +25bp 6.2% / hold 93.8%; by June +25bp 19.9%, +50bp 1.0%, hold 79.2%.
ECB: April hike probability 71% (LSEG via PAP).
ECB: after Schnabel (Fri 27 Mar pm) April +25bp odds fell to ~50%, from a fully priced April hike plus one more a week earlier (PAP week-ahead, 30 Mar).
Fed: hike bets withdrawn; markets shift to pricing the possibility of cuts this year (Jin10 via Odaily; 17:10 Warsaw CEST).
